assessment: This Pantlaza Dinosaurs deck is well-built around 2-Core bracket with good ETB/discover payoffs, ramp, and the Apex Altisaur + Wrathful Raptors combo intact; the changeset focuses on tightening the discover payoff density, shoring up interaction, and smoothing the curve without pushing past bracket 2.

changes.reason: Gishath is an 82%-played Dinosaur commander-level ETB/combat-damage engine that triggers Pantlaza's discover on itself and refills the hand, far outclassing a narrow colorless land.
The deck has no protection for its board wipes or the Apex Altisaur/Wrathful Raptors combo, and Heroic Intervention is a listed near-miss combo piece that also protects against wraths.

cheaper.name: Tamiyo's Safekeeping
cheaper.reason: Cheap single-target protection, much lower cost than Heroic Intervention.

changes.reason: At only 11 spot removal pieces with mostly clunky 3-4 mana answers, adding premier 1-mana removal improves interaction density without changing the Dinosaur plan much since Temple Altisaur's prevention effect is low-impact.

Ghalta is a 73%-played staple huge Dinosaur that is often free to cast off the deck's big creatures and is a strong discover trigger target for Pantlaza, better than a conditional mana land in a 3-color but land-heavy manabase.
Generous Gift is the deck's only flexible removal; Beast Within adds a second instant-speed answer to any permanent type, which this deck currently lacks enough of versus enchantments/planeswalkers.
A land-into-battlefield ramp spell that can fetch a Forest untapped is a strictly better fixing-plus-ramp effect than a tapped triome-style land in a deck already rich in tapped lands.

cheaper.name: Nature's Lore
cheaper.reason: Same effect, slightly cheaper and more widely available.
